newsitem.title: UK: Insurers not off the hook over pensions - Liddell.
newsitem.headline: Insurers not off the hook over pensions - Liddell.

text.p: UK Treasury Minister Helen Liddell said on Tuesday her criticism of two insurance companies' response to her call for action over pensions mis-selling does not mean the rest are off the hook.
The two being singled out did not mean the pressure would be taken off the rest of her list of 24 companies.
"This is one of the worst scandals in financial services," she said.
"No one should assume that because I have accepted their initial comments that they will be off the hook."

Publishing the initial responses of the 24 companies, which set out their strategies for speeding up the review of pension cases, Liddell said she will require monthly reports for the next two or three months.
"If, by the autumn they have not delivered, I will take further action," she said.
Once the initial 24 companies have been dealt with, Liddell will turn her attention to independent financial advisers. "This is the beginning of a saga not the end of it."

Liddell criticised companies who have been hiding behind out dated excuses of occupational pension funds not responding to requests for assistance but said she would take the matter up if there is continuing disruption.
Of the list of 24 companies asked to set out their strategies Sedgewick Group and Legal and General were singled out for failing to understand the Government's determination for quick resolution.

"There has been a lot of buck-passing about the problem", said Liddell. "We asked the companies to acknowledge the scale of the problem. It is no consolation to the 600,000 people (affected) that the companies do not recognise they have a problem."
